runs.name: The AES Corporation; NYSE AES, SEC CIK 0000874761, 10-K filer; electric generation and utilities in the US and abroad, four segments (Renewables, Utilities with AES Indiana and AES Ohio, Energy Infrastructure, New Energy Technologies); signed 2026-03-01 an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Horizon Parent, L.P. (Global Infrastructure Management and EQT Infrastructure VI) at $15.00 a share in cash, approved by stockholders 2026-06-26, CFIUS 2026-08-27, PUCO 2026-09-17, other approvals open, End Date 2027-06-01; the 10-K names no rival, NRG, Vistra and Clearway taken from J.P. Morgan's selected companies in the merger proxy as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q1; INTEGRITY FACTS RECORDED, NOT JUDGED
runs.entry: Price **$14.95** (close 2026-10-16, `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged), $0.05 under the $15.00 cash consideration. Shares 713,438,630 common on the cover of the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (0000874761-26-000144, as of 2026-07-31), `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing, against 859,837,679 issued less 146,679,966 treasury (713,157,713) on that 10-Q's balance sheet; no 8-K after the 10-Q issues common stock. Sovereign **5.43%**, the US Treasury 30-year par yield of 2026-10-16 (issuing authority). Read from the 10-K for FY2025 (0000874761-26-000063), the 10-Ks for FY2024, FY2023, FY2021, FY2019 and FY2017, the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the DEFM14A of 2026-05-15 (0001140361-26-021662), the proxy of 2026-03-20 and the 8-Ks of 2025-03-11 (Item 4.02), 2026-01-16 (Item 2.06), 2026-03-02, 2026-06-16, 2026-06-26, 2026-07-27 (Item 4.01), 2026-08-05, 2026-08-27, 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17; operating cash flow $4,306M and capital spending $5,929M for FY2025 cross-checked against the filed cash-flow statement. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. **Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: the deciding part is Energy Infrastructure, $7,271M or 51% of 2021 to 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of the three earning segments and the largest on any segment boundary (CONVENTION of the run: segment Adjusted EBITDA as the parts measure, the only segment profit Note 19 reports); 12,705 MW of thermal plants in nine countries, 64% of capacity uncontracted or contracted only to 2028 or earlier (Maritza, Southland OTC units, Puerto Rico, Merida, the Dominican plants, Mexico, Colon, Argentina, Angamos), several sold to a state-owned single buyer; its ten-year earnings turn on government recontracting and retirement decisions; the merger proxy says the company publishes no forecasts because of the "uncertainty, unpredictability and subjectivity" of its assumptions and its private forecasts assume no significant regulatory change; bidders with data-room access cited an "inability to reach confidence on a proper valuation", one withdrew over portfolio complexity, one could not support much above $11.48. NATURE, not WORK, because what decides is the governments' decisions, which no filing states; the analyst names WORK as the other reading. Integrity facts recorded, not judged. Facts after the stop (COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE): owner cash 2021 to 2025 after every real cost (emissions allowances, minority distributions, finance-lease principal deducted) -$2,825M a year all-equity, -$3,700M equity-only, negative every year; value range the no-growth case alone, -$115.34 a share all-equity (-$95.50 equity-only); fair price -$82.01 all-equity, not positive (-$51.86 equity-only); with depreciation in place of capital spending, beside, range $5.38 to $15.32, fair -$14.20 all-equity and $14.89 equity-only; no filed maintenance level, so all capital spending charged. Balance sheets 2016 to 2026: debt $19.5B to $32.1B at 2026-06-30 (recourse $6.1B, non-recourse $26.0B), about 6.5 times $4.9B of common equity; minority and tax-equity claims $7.9B; retained earnings in deficit every year-end 2016 to 2023; net income attributable $1,144M against dividends $3,945M over 2016 to 2025; pre-tax coverage 1.05x in 2025. Against the business: the 2024 restatement ($192M of impairment overstated, a material weakness, an adverse internal-control opinion), the Board's statement that without the merger AES needed about $2B of new equity or dividend cuts 2026 to 2030, featured non-GAAP figures including "Adjusted EBITDA with Tax Attributes", pay on non-GAAP targets, a $4B Sinolam suit and the Dominican coal-ash suits. Comparators (XBRL transcription, rivals not checked against filed statements; acquisitions excluded): operating cash less capital spending summed, AES 2016 to 2025 -$10,986M, NRG +$8,499M, Vistra 2017 to 2025 +$11,839M, Clearway +$4,536M. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing filtered on the date showing nine run names of 2026-10-18 (HOKCY, MDU, NJR, NWN, OGS, SR, SWX, UGI, XNGSY), the UGI fold commit subjects, a memory index line, a git status naming AYI and ARCB folders, and after the box a failed commit's git status naming files in other research folders; nothing about AES seen; none used. Commits 9080a701 (template), 7d807e10 (Step 0 and Q1), d50e190e (facts after the stop, self-audit, notes), 7379667c (a proxy excerpt in the ignored cache untracked, committed without a pathspec by the analyst after checking only that deletion was staged), 919739a9 (contamination item 4). Step 0 and Q1 committed together, the file closing at Q1. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's check 28 ids, 0 problems; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` no E-id, no missing id, 34 quoted fragments within reach of an id, 6 flagged by the parser and read by hand as quotations from filings or an unattributed echo, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the text has no question for a stock priced on a pending cash merger; (2) the parts test asks for operating profit and the filer reports only segment Adjusted EBITDA, with a boundary moved inside the window; (3) Q7 silent on minority and tax-equity partners and capital raised by selling stakes ($1.6B a year here); (4) whether section E reaches tax credits sold for cash; (5) WORK or NATURE when the deciding variable is a government's decision; (6) whether a disclosed yearly change in maintenance spending without its level allows the guess. Not armed: box TOO HARD at Q1. Could not get: maintenance spending levels, earnings by plant, the rivals' filed statements, the 10-K/A of 2025-04-11 (not read).
runs.narr: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q1 (The AES Corporation, NYSE AES, generation and utilities in the US and abroad, under a signed $15.00 cash merger with GIP and EQT Infrastructure VI, stockholders approved, other approvals open; the deciding part, Energy Infrastructure at 51% of five-year segment Adjusted EBITDA, is 12,705 MW of thermal plants in nine countries, 64% uncontracted or contracted only to 2028 or earlier, whose ten-year earnings turn on government recontracting and retirement decisions the insiders do not forecast; integrity facts recorded, not judged. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash -$2,825M a year all-equity, negative every year 2021 to 2025; fair price -$82.01 all-equity, not positive, at $14.95; debt $32.1B against $4.9B of common equity; the 2024 restatement and material weakness. Not armed. No citation slip. Framework gaps for the operator: a stock priced on a pending cash merger, the parts test where only Adjusted EBITDA is reported, minority and tax-equity partners in Q7, tax credits sold for cash under section E, WORK or NATURE for a government's decision, a maintenance change without a level.)
